ch9_lab_datatypes.title: Quick Check: Variables, Data Types & Operators

questions.q: Which keyword should you use to declare a variable that is expected to change, like a running shopping cart total?
What is the result of the expression 5 === "5"?
options: true, because both represent the number 5
false, because strict equality checks both value AND data type, and one is a Number while the other is a String
true, because JavaScript automatically converts strings to numbers

questions.q: Due to JavaScript's type coercion, what is the result of '5' + 5?
options: "55" (the number is converted to a string and glued on)
An error, since you can't mix strings and numbers

questions.q: What is the difference between declaring a function and calling a function?
options: Declaring writes out the instructions (the recipe); calling actually executes those instructions (cooking the meal)
Declaring runs the code immediately; calling just saves it for later
Calling a function deletes it after use

questions.q: A function calculates a total but has no return statement. If you store its output in a variable and log it, what will print?
options: undefined, because without return the result never gets sent back out

questions.q: A variable is declared with let INSIDE a function. Can you access that variable from code OUTSIDE the function?
options: Yes, all variables are always global
No -- it has Local Scope, so using it outside the function throws a ReferenceError
Yes, but only if you use const instead of let

options: It deletes the form from the page
It stops the browser's default action (refreshing/submitting the page) so your JS can handle it instead
It prevents the event listener from ever running again
